question: What is the primary objective of orienting a newly admitted patient to the ward?

options.A: To complete the formal medical discharge summary
options.B: To restrict family visiting hours permanently
options.C: To immediately collect payment for hospital services
options.D: To reduce anxiety and build trust in the healthcare team

explanation: A warm reception and clear orientation help lower the psychological stress associated with hospitalization, fostering a therapeutic nurse-patient relationship. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which action should be prioritized first when a new patient arrives at the nursing station?

options.A: Inventorying all personal belongings in front of visitors
options.B: Administering the evening dose of prescribed sedatives
options.C: Greeting the patient by name and offering a welcoming environment
options.D: Completing the physical examination and diagnostic workup

explanation: Establishing immediate human contact and a welcoming atmosphere creates safety and comfort before diving into complex clinical tasks. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h1)

question: An admission that is planned in advance for an elective surgical procedure is classified as which type?
explanation: Routine admissions are scheduled ahead of time, allowing the ward staff and patient to prepare adequately. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the immediate clinical priority when managing an emergency admission?

options.A: Immediate patient stabilization and life support
options.B: Finalizing the formal financial billing agreement
options.C: Inventorying all personal valuable items and cash
options.D: Conducting a detailed social history interview

explanation: In emergency scenarios, clinical stabilization of acute physiological threats always supersedes routine administrative processes. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which document is primarily used to formally record the initial entry of a patient's arrival into the unit?
explanation: The ward register maintains a chronological log of all admissions, transfers, and discharges occurring within that specific unit. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: How should a nurse legally manage a patient's valuable jewelry upon admission if family members are unavailable?

options.A: Record them on a property form and secure them in the hospital safe
options.B: Keep them at the bedside locker under the patient's pillow
options.C: Wear them on duty to prevent theft by other patients
options.D: Discard them in the clinical waste bin as unallowed items

explanation: Valuables must be formally documented and locked away in institutional safe custody to prevent loss and protect the facility from liability. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a formal patient referral letter?

options.A: To provide a permanent prescription for over-the-counter medications
options.B: To discharge the patient completely from all healthcare follow-ups
options.C: To communicate clinical history and the reason for transfer to receiving staff
options.D: To serve as a definitive receipt for hospital billing and NHIS payments

explanation: The referral letter ensures continuity of care by providing the receiving team with essential clinical background and the rationale for escalation. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: Which action must a nurse perform BEFORE dispatching a patient on inter-facility referral?

options.A: Ensure the patient has paid all outstanding pharmacy bills in full
options.B: Remove all intravenous cannulas to prevent injury during transport
options.C: Confirm bed availability and acceptance with the receiving facility
options.D: Request the patient walk independently to the transport vehicle

explanation: Pre-transit communication prevents delays upon arrival and ensures the receiving unit is prepared to manage the specific acuity of the incoming patient. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: Moving a patient from the surgical ward to the radiology department for a CT scan is an example of what type of movement?
explanation: An intra-facility transfer refers to moving a patient between different units or departments within the exact same hospital campus. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: A critically ill patient is being transferred from a rural cottage hospital to a federal teaching hospital. What is the most crucial requirement during transit?

options.A: Carrying a copy of the hospital menu and visiting guidelines
options.B: Traveling without an escort to maximize ambulance seat space
options.C: Immediate settlement of all administrative discharge fees
options.D: Continuous monitoring and availability of emergency life support

explanation: Critically ill patients remain vulnerable during transit and require continuous observation and active life-support readiness. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h5)

question: At what point in the hospital stay should discharge planning ideally begin?

options.B: After the doctor signs the discharge summary
options.D: When the patient requests their bill

explanation: Early discharge planning prevents unnecessary delays, identifies potential post-discharge barriers, and ensures adequate preparation. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which factor is most vital to evaluate when planning the discharge of an elderly stroke patient?

options.A: Availability of private security guards at the residence
options.B: The patient's personal preference for ward interior paint
options.C: The distance to the nearest commercial shopping mall
options.D: Home environment and availability of family caregivers

explanation: Assessing the home setup and caregiver support ensures the patient can manage activities of daily living safely outside the hospital. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the appropriate nursing action when a competent patient insists on leaving the hospital Against Medical Advice (DAMA)?

options.A: Physically lock the ward exit doors to prevent the patient from escaping
options.B: Call the local police department to arrest the patient immediately
options.C: Ignore the request and withhold all personal clothing and belongings
options.D: Inform the physician, explain the risks, and have the patient sign a DAMA form

explanation: Informed refusal is a patient right; documenting the risk discussion and securing a signature protects both the patient and the institution legally. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which task is NOT part of the nurse's final responsibilities during a routine patient discharge?

options.A: Prescribing new specialized medications independently without medical review
options.B: Ensuring the bed space is cleaned and prepared for a new admission
options.C: Providing health education on home care and warning signs
options.D: Verifying that all personal belongings and valuables are returned

explanation: Prescribing medications falls outside the independent nursing scope of practice and requires a licensed medical practitioner's order. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h7)
